items.title: CSS-Tricks has a new owner
items.blurb: Yes, I've got the keys to the castle, so to speak. And, even after 12 years of working on the site, I'll admit I'm a little overwhelmed and nervous about that.

items.title: Safari 27.1 previews the Device Posture and Viewport Segments APIs
items.blurb: Today iPhone Duo arrives, and with it, Safari 27.1.

items.title: Websites Should Be Printable
items.blurb: A place for the personal blog, projects, and wanderings of Brennen Puth.

items.title: Would You Let Your AI Agent Grade Its Own Homework?
items.blurb: Meticulous auto-generates and auto-maintains visual frontend browser tests, providing a level of coverage that is unattainable with manually written tests.

items.title: Building an Isolated Preview for AI-Generated HTML
items.blurb: An iframe with srcdoc feels like a safe place to render HTML a model wrote. It isn't. Three tests show how the preview can read your page, escape the frame, and phone home, and four layers of protection close each hole.

items.title: HTML-in-Canvas: Interactive DOM Inside 2D, WebGL and WebGPU Canvases
items.blurb: Chrome 157 ships the HTML-in-Canvas API, letting you render live, interactive, and accessible DOM subtrees into 2D, WebGL, and WebGPU canvases.
